1.title: Trouble in the Empire
1.sourceFile: Romance of the Three Kingdoms 1. Trouble in the Empire.pdf

paragraphs.text: Long ago, Liu Bang founded the Han dynasty and united all of China. For four hundred years, people lived peacefully. But in the Year 168, things began to change. There was a new ruler, Emperor Ling. He was just 12 years old, and court officials took advantage of this. They seized power and made themselves richer. Then a famine swept across the land. Chaos was returning . . .

In a small village, a young man was selling straw shoes. His name was Liu Bei. He was a distant relative of the Hans, but he’d spent his life in poverty. As a child, he’d often played under a huge mulberry tree by his house. The tree’s branches formed a dense canopy. It looked like the canopy on the emperor’s carriage.

Some people thought it was a sign. They believed Liu Bei was destined for greatness. But now he was 28 years old and supporting his elderly mother. “I haven’t sold a pair of shoes in days,” Liu Bei thought. “And we have almost no food.” A woman stopped to look at the shoes. Liu Bei jumped to his feet. “Good morning!

Would you like to buy—” “No, thank you.” The woman walked away. Liu Bei sat down and sighed. In another village a man named Zhang Jue was hungry—and angry. He took a walk in the mountains to clear his mind.

An old man approached him. They talked for a bit. Then the man gave him a book, The Peaceful Way for the Future. “It will help you,” the man said. “But, remember, you must always practice compassion. Otherwise bad things will happen to you.” The old man vanished. Zhang Jue opened the book and gasped. “This book is filled with magic spells!”

He studied the book. In time he mastered its secrets, learning how to heal people and control the weather. With these powers, he could stop all suffering! Zhang Jue went back to his village and raised his hands. People stopped to watch. The sky grew dark. Clouds rolled in. Rain splashed down. The crowd gasped.

“He knows magic!” “That rain will save our crops!” Zhang Jue traveled to other villages. Everywhere he went, he conjured rain and healed the sick. People began to follow him, and their numbers quickly increased. This new power twisted Zhang Jue’s mind. He forgot about the old man’s warning. He turned his back on compassion and focused

on power instead. “ I ’ llwipeouttheHans , ” ZhangJue thought eagerly. “I’ll rule over everyone!” He turned his followers into an army. They wore yellow turbans. Under Zhang Jue’s command, they attacked soldiers. They burned the homes of anyone loyal to the Hans. News of their terror spread fast. One day a man and his son were tending

their garden. Shouts suddenly rang out. Smoke rose from a house. “The Yellow Turbans are attacking,” the man whispered. “We must leave.” “But, Father!” the boy said. “We don’t even have our shoes.” “Come! Now!” The man picked up his boy and ran. They hid in the forest and waited for

nightfall. Relying on the moon for light, they walked all night. The next morning they arrived in a village. Their feet were bruised and bloody when they spotted a young man selling shoes. They didn’t know this, but the young man was about to help them. He would also change China forever.

2.title: Frightening Tales
2.sourceFile: Romance of the Three Kingdoms 2. Frightening Tales.pdf

paragraphs.text: Liu Bei’s heart sank at the sight of this poor man and child. What horrors had they been through? The man pulled some coins from his pocket. “Please, sir. I . . . I need a pair of shoes.” Liu Bei nodded. “Of course. I have plenty of them.” The child tugged the man’s sleeve. “Father, I need a pair too!”

The man sighed. “I can’t afford two pairs, son. I need shoes so I can find work.” Liu Bei felt awful. “I have no reason to pity myself,” he thought. “These two have suffered much more than I.” He cleared his throat. “Sir, may I ask what happened to you?” “Our village was destroyed,” the man said. “Vicious brutes attacked people and burned

every home. My son and I barely escaped.” Liu Bei gasped. “Who were the attackers?” The man glanced nervously from side to side before whispering, “The Yellow Turban Rebels.” “I’ve heard of them,” Liu Bei said. “They’re growing more powerful and want to overthrow the Hans.” The man counted his coins. “I hope I have enough money.”

“You definitely do!” Liu Bei said quickly. “My shoes only cost one coin.” The man raised an eyebrow. “Your shoes appear to be of good quality. Surely they cost more than a single coin?” “Nope!” Liu Bei smiled. “In fact, one coin can buy you two pairs.” He looked at the boy’s feet and picked out a pair of shoes. “I believe these will fit you.”

The boy grinned. “Thank you!” Tears filled the man’s eyes. “Are you sure?” “Absolutely,” Liu Bei said. “You and your son have suffered enough. I’m happy to help.” The man gave Liu Bei a coin. Then he bowed his head. “You are a kind man. If only there were more people like you in this world.” “You’re welcome,” Liu Bei said.

Over the next few days, more people arrived in Liu Bei’s village. They all brought their own frightening tales of the Yellow Turban Rebellion. People gathered to hear them. “Their leader, Zhang Jue, is a magician!” an old man said. “He can control the weather and—”

A villager cried. “Nonsense!” “Shush!” a woman said. “Let him tell his story!” The old man took a breath. “The Yellow Turban traitors arrived at my village with swords and torches. Han soldiers tried to defend our homes. At one point, it seemed like they might win. But then . . .” The man’s voice lowered to a whisper. “Zhang Jue appeared.”

Liu Bei moved closer. Theoldmancontinued . “ ZhangJue held up his arms. Rain poured down. Wind howled. A moment later the imperial soldiers were gone!” The crowd gasped. “The Yellow Turbans have attacked many other villages since then,” the man said. “In one, the soldiers didn’t even fight back. They

just ran when they saw the Yellow Turbans.” ThenextdayLiuBeisawposters everywhere in the village. He went over to read one. It was a message from the local governor, Liu Yan. We mustdefeatthe Ye llow Tu rban Rebellion. I need all healthy men to form armies and fight for the Hans.

“I would gladly fight for my emperor,” Liu Bei thought. “But I’m poor—and it costs money to form an army.” He thought about how that poor man and his son had suffered. Liu Bei shook his head and sighed. Suddenly a voice behind him boomed. “All you can do is sigh? How useless!”

3.title: Two Fierce Men
3.sourceFile: Romance of the Three Kingdoms 3. Two Fierce Men.pdf

paragraphs.text: Liu Bei spun around and saw a fierce- looking man. He was tall with a wild beard. His eyes were sharp—like the eyes of a panther. “You should fight the Yellow Turbans instead of just sighing about the problem.” The man stepped closer. “Or are you thinking about joining the rebellion?” “No,” Liu Bei said. “I am loyal to Emperor

Ling. I only sighed because I’m frustrated. My name is Liu Bei. And as a distant relative of the emperor, it’s my duty to fight for the Han. But I have no money to raise an army.” A wide grin spread across the man’s face. “We should work together!” “Are you serious?” Liu Bei did not expect this! The man nodded. “My name is Zhang Fei.

My family has lots of money. I can pay for weapons, armor, horses, food . . . everything we’ll need. And you’re related to the Hans! We’ll have no problem recruiting soldiers if you’re leading the army.” Liu Bei bowed. “Zhang Fei, I would be delighted to work with you. We must put together a plan.” “Excellent!” Zhang Fei said.

Later the two men went to a pub. At the entrance a woman was scolding a man. “I can’t believe you won’t help the emperor. You should be ashamed.” “I’m not ashamed,” the man said. “I’m going to join the Yellow Turbans.” Zhang Fei stomped over. “What did you say?” The man folded his arms. “You heard

me.” Zhang Fei held up his spear. “Say it again!” The man pulled out a knife. “I’m going to join the—” Whoosh! Zhang Fei swung his weapon, knocking the knife to the ground. He swung again and hit the man on the head with the spear’s wooden shaft. Bonk!

“Ouch!” The man turned and ran out of the village. The woman looked at Zhang Fei. “I’m so happy to see someone who is against the Yellow Turbans.” Zhang Fei bowed. Then he turned to Liu Bei. “We’re already winning.” The two men laughed and went into the pub. They sat down at a table in the corner.

The owner brought them a drink. “There’s no charge for this. I saw how you handled that traitor outside.” Zhang Fei nodded. “Thank you.” The owner hurried over to another table. “We’ll need a lot of soldiers,” Liu Bei said. “I’m sure you can train them.” “Of course!” Zhang Fei took a swig of his drink. “I’m quite strong—never lost a fight

in my life. I can’t wait to fight those Yellow Turban good-for-nothings. I’ll destroy them all!” “Not if I destroy them first!” someone said. Liu Bei looked up and saw another fierce- looking man. He was even taller than Zhang Fei, with a much longer beard. “Who are you?” Zhang Fei asked.

“My name is Guan Yu. I arrived in this village hoping to join an army.” The man puffed out his chest. “I, too, want to wipe out the Yellow Turbans.” “Excellent!” Liu Bei stood up. “I’m Liu Bei, and this is Zhang Fei. He is—” “The greatest fighter in the land!” Zhang Fei said. Guan Yu scoffed. “Well, I doubt that,
because I am the greatest fighter in the land.” He narrowed his eyes. “I’m sure I could beat you.” Zhang Fei’s face filled with rage. He jumped to his feet and drew his spear!

"There's no way you can beat me!" Zhang Fei glared at Guan Yu. Guan Yu began to draw his spear. Liu Bei got between the two men. "Please stop. You don't need to fight!" Zhang Fei pushed him away. The pub fell silent as the two men stared into each other's eyes. The owner looked worried. "I don't want anyone to get hurt." "Fine!" Zhang Fei pointed at his weapon. "We'll fight like this, with our blades covered."

He placed his feet apart, with his covered spear held out to his side. Guan Yu crouched low. His spear pointed directly at Zhang Fei. Suddenly he lunged forward, striking with fury! Zhang Fei moved like a cat, quickly sidestepping Guan Yu's attack. His weapon swept through the air. Guan Yu immediately bent far backward. Zhang Fei's spear swiped clear over his head. A second later Guan Yu was upright. He brought his spear down with tremendous force. Zhang Fei spun out of the way. Guan Yu's spear broke a table in two.

The person at the next table fell from his bench. "Whoa!" The owner gasped. "My table!" The fight between Zhang Fei and Guan Yu moved around the pub. Their weapons smashed into each other again and again. Bam! Smack! Tables and benches broke. Customers hid in corners. The owner held his head in his hands. "My poor pub." Liu Bei frowned. "This is completely unnecessary."

Finally Guan Yu held up a hand. "Let's stop." Zhang Fei lowered his spear and grinned. "So I won?" "Of course not!" Guan Yu put down his weapon. "But I didn't win either. I have fought many men in my life. Nobody was nearly as tough as you. I believe we are equals." Zhang Fei rubbed his chin. Then he put his spear away too. "Yes, I believe you are right." The two men bowed to each other.

Afterward they looked at the mess. Zhang Fei approached the pub's owner. "Please accept my apology." He handed the man some money. "And please accept this. I believe it will pay for all the repairs." He looked around. "I will also pay for everyone's meals." The customers cheered. Liu Bei was relieved. "It was pointless for you two to fight one another," he said. "We should be fighting together." Guan Yu nodded. "I agree." "Let's go to my home," Zhang Fei said. "We can discuss our plans for wiping out the Yellow Turban rebels—together!"

A magnificent peach orchard stood behind Zhang Fei's house. Flowers bloomed on every branch. The three men sat at a table. Zhang Fei poured tea. Liu Bei took a sip. "It's strange. But it feels as if we were meant to meet one another." "I know what you mean," Guan Yu said. "We come from different families. But I feel as if we are brothers." Zhang Fei put down his cup. "Let's make an oath—an oath that cannot be broken."

There and then, the three men swore a sacred vow. We are Liu Bei, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei. We will restore the Han Dynasty and protect the common people. If one of us is in danger, the others will help him. We shall fight together and we shall die together. If we fail to uphold this oath, let Heaven punish us. From here on, we shall be sworn oath brothers!

After the three men swore their oath, they named Liu Bei as their leader. This made sense because royal blood flowed through his veins. He was a moral and humble man with no desire to rule over others. And sometimes that is exactly what is needed in a leader. The next day Liu Bei stood in a village square. Beside him were his two oath brothers. A few people wandered over to hear what this young man had to say. "I'm recruiting soldiers to fight the Yellow Turban rebels!" Liu Bei said.

One man called out, "Why should we fight them?" Zhang Fei's eyes filled with rage. He stepped forward, but Liu Bei held up a hand. "I will tell you why," Liu Bei said. "Their leader, Zhang Jue, is a fraud." A few people gasped. Liu Bei continued. "Zhang Jue says he'll end corruption. He'll free everyone from the Hans." "That's right!" someone said. Zhang Fei snorted.

"Has he actually done that?" Liu Bei asked. Nobody answered. "He has not," Liu Bei said. "Instead he and his army have ransacked villages! They've burned homes! They've attacked innocent people! Does that sound like freedom?" A few people muttered to each other. "Zhang Jue learned how to use powerful magic," Liu Bei said. "Has he shared that knowledge with anyone?" "No," someone said. Liu Bei shook his head. "Zhang Jue doesn't want to help anyone. He doesn't want to share anything. He only wants one thing—power!" He held up his hands. "I, on the other hand, have no interest in power. I just want regular people like us to live peacefully and have enough food."

The crowd cheered. A number of people stepped forward, ready to join Liu Bei's army. Liu Bei made the same speech in other villages. And in each one, more people joined the cause. In a stable an old man was brushing a horse. A man entered. "I need horses for Liu Bei's army." He handed the old man a heavy bag of coins. "Give me as many horses as you can spare!"

A metalsmith was busy at his forge when a man burst in. "Liu Bei needs weapons and armor for five hundred soldiers!" The metalsmith raised an eyebrow. "That will cost a fortune." "Don't worry about the cost." The man held out a heavy bag of coins. "Zhang Fei will pay for it all!" The metalsmith got right to work. Before long, Liu Bei's army had all the weapons and armor they needed. The metalsmith even made special weapons for the three oath brothers. Liu Bei got a pair of double-edged blades. Zhang Fei got a long spear. And Guan Yu got a spear with a curved blade, which he named the Green Dragon Crescent Blade.

The local governor, Liu Yan, was working at his desk. An officer hurried in. "Sir! Yellow Turbans are attacking the city of Qingzhou!" Liu Yan stood up. "Get the troops ready!" "Yes, sir!" The officer hurried away. Liu Yan put on his helmet and armor. He headed outside. When he saw the small number of men, he gulped. "Where are all the soldiers?" The officer bit his lip. "These are the only men who signed up, sir. People are scared to fight." Liu Yan sighed. "It's hopeless then. We can't fight the Yellow Turbans with such a small group."
Just then the earth rumbled and shook with the sound of horses. The color drained from Liu Yan's face. "An army is approaching!"

Liu Yan held his breath as hundreds of armed soldiers arrived. Their sharp swords and spears sparkled in the morning sun. Three men led the army. Two looked like beasts, with wild beards and fierce eyes. The one in the middle, however, had a kind face. The men got down from their horses and bowed. "I am Liu Bei," the kind-looking man said. "And these are my oath brothers, Zhang Fei and Guan Yu. We are here to fight the Yellow Turbans." Liu Yan breathed a sigh of relief. "Your timing could not be better. The Yellow Turbans are currently attacking the city of Qingzhou." "Good!" Zhang Fei growled. "I'm in the mood to fight!" Everyone cheered.

Qingzhou sat on top of a large hill. A wall surrounded the city. Liu Bei saw Yellow Turbans ramming a huge door with a battering ram. Others were trying to scale the wall with ladders. Imperial archers stood on the wall, firing arrows at the rebels. The archers were holding off the attack for now. But those arrows wouldn't last forever.

Liu Bei raised a sword. "Attack!" He and his army charged up the hill. Before they reached the top, they were met with the spears of Yellow Turbans. Metal clashed, horses reared up, and men fell. Zhang Fei stabbed his spear up toward the enemy. "Scoundrels!" Guan Yu bravely swung the Green Dragon Crescent Blade. "Traitors!" But the Yellow Turbans held the higher ground, making it impossible to reach the top. Many of Liu Bei's soldiers fell and did not get back up. The sight nearly broke Liu Bei's heart. "Those soldiers trusted me," he thought. "And I've led them to their doom." He turned to his oath brothers. "We're losing too many soldiers. We must turn back." The two men nodded. "Retreat!"

The army ran back down the hill. Up above, Yellow Turbans laughed. "Cowards!" Zhang Fei fumed. "I'm not a coward!" "Ignore them," Guan Yu said. "We're not giving up," Liu Bei said. "But we need a different plan if we want to win this battle. The Yellow Turbans have the advantage of higher ground." Guan Yu looked up at the hill. "We must remove that advantage." Zhang Fei folded his arms. "How?" Liu Bei tapped his chin. "I have a plan. But first we must move our camp. I don't want the Yellow Turbans to see what we're doing."

The morning air was chilly as Liu Bei climbed onto his horse. Less than a third of his army was gathered in front of him. Zhang Fei and Guan Yu were nowhere to be seen. Liu Bei led the soldiers back toward the hill. He looked up at the Yellow Turbans and raised a sword. "Attack!" Once again Liu Bei and his brave soldiers charged up the slope. The sound of clashing steel filled the air as the two armies fought. Then Liu Bei yelled, "Retreat!" His army turned around and raced back down the hill. "Don't let them get away this time!" a Yellow Turban commander shouted. "We have them outnumbered!" Liu Bei and his soldiers reached the bottom and continued across the field. The Yellow Turbans followed. "Good," Liu Bei thought, hiding a grin. "My plan is working."

Soon they were far from the hill. Liu Bei ordered his men to spin around. The Yellow Turbans slowed down, and the two armies faced one another. The rebel commander laughed. "What a pitiful little army. We'll destroy all of you!"
